feedback.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$  what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\frac{\pi }{6}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/00d540b1f6412e4af2617452fbf0c58750d01e844d89d0d92cfacc0cb3e45e32.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are $x=\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{5\pi }{6}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}{x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{6}\cdot \frac{5\pi }{6}=\frac{5{\pi }^{2}}{36}.
$$
